newsitem.title: UK: UK finance directors split over Social Chapter.
newsitem.headline: UK finance directors split over Social Chapter.

text.p: British financial directors are split over the effects of the government signing up for the European Union Social Chapter, a survey out on Thursday shows.
Reed Accountancy Personnel surveyed 200 finance directors and found 58 percent believe it would not hit their business while 42 percent said it would.
Queen Elizabeth, making a formal speech to open the parliament elected on May 1, confirmed the new Labour government would sign the Social Chapter.
A government note accompanying the Queen's speech said the protocol only boasted two directives -- on parental leave and consultation rights for employees of multinational companies.
"Should any further legislative proposals be made, the government would make sure that the issues of employability and competitiveness were central to the decision-making process," it said.
The Reed survey found 36 percent of finance directors thought the Social Chapter's provisions would eventually have been introduced under a Labour or Conservative government.
But they were worried that the protocol could open the way for potentially damaging legislation in the future.
However, 22 percent of the directors said the Social Chapter would have a positive effect on their businesses and the UK economy as a whole.
The 42 percent who saw it hurting business as it stands feared increased costs and bureaucracy.

"A small majority of financial directors believe that signing up to the Social Chapter, as it now stands, will not have any adverse effect on their businesses, although some are concerned about possible future legislation that we may be tying ourselves into by signing up," said David Callaghan, director of Reed Accountancy Personnel.
He said the survey also highlighted the level of confusion about what the Social Chapter actually involved. "This is a matter which clearly needs to be addressed," Callaghan said.
